After: D is gone, shown dashed, and its edge has been rerouted to A, so a new accent edge joins A and E." width="100%"} Creates a new graph where node `node_2` is removed and all its edges are redirected to node `node_1`. If there was an edge between `node_1` and `node_2`, it becomes a self-loop on `node_1` (unless `self_loops=False`). This operation does not modify the original graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to keep (node ID or label). All edges from `node_2` will be redirected here. [node_2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to merge into `node_1` (node ID or label). This node will be removed. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), edges between `node_1` and `node_2` become self-loops on `node_1`. If `False`, such edges are removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `node_2` contracted into `node_1`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either node does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `node_1` and `node_2` are the same node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Contraction is a fundamental graph-minor operation: the surviving node $u$ inherits every edge incident to $v$, and any $u$-$v$ edge becomes a self-loop on $u$ unless `self_loops=False` suppresses it. The traversal costs $O(E)$ time and produces a fresh graph, so the original is left intact. Node $u$ keeps its label and attributes, and edge weights carry through unchanged. Edges at $u$ that end up joining the same pair of nodes collapse into the first of them, which keeps its ID, weight and attributes, so $u$ is left with at most one edge to each neighbor (one in each direction on a directed graph) and at most one self-loop. Edges between other nodes, parallel ones included, are kept as they are. Contraction is what drives the aggregation phase of Louvain community detection and underpins the reduced graphs used in minor-based algorithms like planarity testing. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d696cdf7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a path: A -- B -- C -- D g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) result = g.contract_nodes("A", "B") result.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: "B" is gone entirely -- its connections were redirected to "A" instead: ::: {#889f7960 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.has_node("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: When the two merged nodes were already connected to each other, that edge becomes a self-loop on the surviving node -- unless `self_loops=False` removes it instead: ::: {#cf8a48f9 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) with_loop = g.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=True) without_loop = g.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=False) with_loop.count_all_loops(), without_loop.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (1, 0) ``` ::: ::: This makes contraction a convenient way to simplify a graph by merging nodes that should be treated as one -- for example, collapsing two adjacent nodes of a path: ::: {#73925dcb .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(5) # 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 simplified = g.contract_nodes(2, 3) simplified.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
